info.name: ProctorAI - Complaint Management API
info.description:
Reactive Spring microservices behind the API gateway (default http://localhost:7050).

**Quick start**
1. Import this collection and the `ProctorAI Local` environment, then select the environment.
2. Start the stack: `./gradlew runAll` (Postgres, MinIO and Redis are started for you).
3. Run **Auth / Login (admin)**. The httpOnly `token` (access) and `refresh_token` cookies are stored in Postman's cookie jar.
4. Run requests top to bottom: create requests save ids (userId, roleId, departmentId, complaintId, fileId, notificationId ...) into collection variables.

**Sessions.** The access token is short lived (JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRE_IN_SEC). When a request returns 401 the collection tries `POST /auth/refresh` automatically and tells you to re-send. Use the *body delivery* login/refresh requests for clients without cookies.

**Authorization** is enforced by PostgreSQL row level security and runtime roles/permissions: 404 can mean 'not visible to you', 403 means 'visible but not allowed'.

**Folders**: Health, Auth, Users, Roles & Permissions, Departments, Custom Fields, Complaints (comments, history, stats), Files (S3 presigned upload/download), Notifications (inbox, realtime SSE, devices, group send, admin FCM integration), Face Recognition (enroll, recognize, manage enrollments).

**Admin web panel** for push integration: open {{baseUrl}}/notifications/panel in a browser.

request.description: Rotates the refresh token: reads the `refresh_token` cookie (or a JSON body `{"refreshToken": "..."}`), returns a new access token and a NEW refresh token, and sets both cookies. Reusing an already-used refresh token revokes the whole session family. Call this when an API request returns 401 because the access token expired.

request.description: Same as above, but tokens are also returned in the JSON body (accessToken, refreshToken) for clients that cannot use cookies.

item.description: Two cookies: `token` (access JWT, short lived) and `refresh_token` (opaque, rotated on every refresh, only sent to /auth). Lifetimes come from JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRE_IN_SEC and JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRE_IN_SEC. `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` is also accepted.

item.name: Create shared complaint about several people

request.description: One complaint naming several people. `studentId` is the main person (department routing uses their department); `subjectIds` lists the others. Everyone named can see the complaint, comment on it and is notified. Requires `complaints:write` with department or all scope; the caller must be able to see every person. The response `subjects` lists everyone the complaint is about.

exec: if (pm.response.code < 300) { try { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.collectionVariables.set('complaintId', b.id); pm.test('Lists every subject', function () { pm.expect(b.subjects.length).to.be.at.least(1); }); } catch (e) {} }

item.name: Face Recognition
item.description: Self-hosted ONNX detection (SCRFD) + recognition (ArcFace); enrolled embeddings are matched via pgvector. `faceImageBase64` can be a raw base64 string or a full `data:image/...;base64,...` URL - both are accepted. Enroll/update/delete are scoped (own/department/all) per the caller's `face_recognition` permission; recognize only needs `face_recognition:read`.

request.description: Enrolls the logged-in user's own face. Works for anyone with `face_recognition:write` at any scope (own/department/all).
Enrolls another user's face. Requires `face_recognition:write` scoped to `department` (target shares a department with the caller) or `all`.

Detects every face in the photo and matches each against enrolled users the caller can see. Returns the decoded image as a clean base64 PNG with its `width` and `height`, plus a bounding box (in image pixels) and match per face, so clients draw their own overlay. Every scan is written to the face activity log. Requires `face_recognition:read`.

Same as photo recognition but for camera frames: send `source: camera`. The response `image` is empty (the client already shows the video) while `width`, `height` and the boxes are returned. Each person is written to the activity log at most once a minute per viewer. Requires `face_live_recognition:read`.
Lists everyone currently enrolled (name, email, enrolledAt). Requires `face_recognition:read`.
Removes the logged-in user's own enrollment.
Removes another user's enrollment. Requires `face_recognition:write`/`delete` scoped to `department` or `all`.
Lets the user enroll or replace their own face again after using up their self-enrollment attempts. Requires `face_enroll_lock:update` for that user.

Who scanned or enrolled whom, and when. Filter with `event` (recognize, live_recognize, enroll, replace, remove, unlock, bulk_import) and `subjectId`. Requires `face_audit:read`; the scope decides whose activity is visible.
Template that maps photo file names to user emails for a ZIP import. `format` is `csv` or `xlsx`. Requires `face_import:read`.
Upload a ZIP containing face photos plus the filled template. Returns 202 with a `processId`; progress is streamed to the uploader in realtime. Requires `face_import:write`.

formdata.description: ZIP archive with photos and the mapping file

item.name: System Monitor
item.description: Live resource usage of the host, every service, PostgreSQL, Redis and file storage. Requires `system_monitor:read`.

request.description: Latest snapshot plus up to 5 minutes of history points (sampled every 2 seconds): host CPU, memory, disks and network, per-service JVM and traffic figures, database, cache and storage.

exec: if (pm.response.code === 200) { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.test('Has a latest snapshot', function () { pm.expect(b.latest).to.be.an('object'); }); }

request.description: Server-sent events: one `overview` event, then a `snapshot` event every 2 seconds and a `heartbeat` every 15 seconds. The stream ends if the caller loses `system_monitor:read`. Postman shows events as they arrive.

exec: // When the access token expired, refresh it once and ask the user to re-send.
pm.sendRequest({ url: pm.variables.get('baseUrl') + '/auth/refresh', method: 'POST' }, function (err, res) {
if (!err && res.code === 200) { console.log('Access token refreshed - send the request again.'); }
else { console.log('Session expired - run Auth / Login.'); }
